chunks: Ghiyāth ibn Ibrāhīm narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from ʿAlī عليه السلام:

Regarding two men between whom there is property: some of it is in their possession and some of it is absent from them. They divided what was in their possession, and each one assigned his share. Then one of them received his share, while the other did not receive his. He said: Whatever one of them receives is between them both, and whatever is lost is between them both.

key_terms.بِنَصِيبِهِ: with his allotted share or portion
key_terms.غَائِبٌ: property absent and not currently in hand
key_terms.فَاقْتَسَمَا: they divided the property between themselves
key_terms.فَقَبَضَ: then he took possession or collected
key_terms.مَالٌ: jointly owned property or wealth under discussion

ai.seo_question: How is loss or recovery handled when two partners divide jointly owned property but some of it is still absent?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about jointly owned property when partners divide what is presently available while other portions remain outstanding. If one partner later receives something or if some of the absent property is lost, both the gain and the loss remain shared between them according to their joint entitlement.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3406 - Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) from his father, Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), from his forefathers, from Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as):

Regarding two men who share property-some of it is in their possession, and some is absent-so they divide what is in their possession, and each one assigns his share. One of them collects his share, but the other does not collect his share.
Imam Ali (as) said: "Whatever is collected by one of them is shared between them, and whatever is lost is also shared between them."
